violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: Employee observed donning gloves without washing hands first. A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands.
violations.corrective_action: Corrected by instruction/discussion. ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: Raw chicken observed over ready-to-eat vegetables in 1dr. upright and raw bacon observed over lettuce in 2dr. Uprt.
violations.corrective_action: Corrected by relocation. Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to-eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: container of turkey x2 and shredded lettuce observed at 47, 47 and 49F respectively in the prep refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Corrected by discarding. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. EHS advised CFM to relocate all TCS foods to another unit as the prep refrigerator may not be capable of maintaining foods at 41F or below. Advised CFM to monitor refrigerator throughout the day and if found not operational, to contact a technician to service the refrigerator. SULLY CAFE (Inspection Date: 08/24/2026) Page 2 of 4

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site (and commercial foods) is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation/opening and was not observed to be date marked: turkey, potatoes, cut deli meats, cheese. No date marking method observed.
violations.corrective_action: Corrected by instruction. CFM began date marking when asked during time of inspection. Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Restricted Use Pesticide, Conditions of use
violations.observation: Container of RAID observed in the back kitchen area.
violations.corrective_action: CFM removed the RAID. Discussed proper pest control processes. Because of their toxicity, restricted use pesticides must be applied by a certified pesticide applicator to prevent injury and contamination.

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: scrapple observed thawing on counter.
violations.corrective_action: Scrapple was moved to the refrigerator for thawing. Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process.

violations.title: Food Packaged, Labeled per Law
violations.observation: Pastries and cookies made off-site at a manufacturing plant are not labeled with ingredients. Food packaged in the establishment is not labeled in accordance with Law.
violations.corrective_action: Obtain ingredients as discussed and keep on site for customer and Health Department review. Food packaged in a food establishment shall be labeled as specified in Law including 21 CFR 101 - Food labeling, and 9 CFR 317 Labeling, marking devices, and containers.
